program.administering_org: New Jersey Department of Human Services, Division of Family Development
program.description: New Jersey's Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program pays monthly food benefits onto a Families First card that can be used to buy groceries. Eligibility depends on household size, gross monthly income and resources; New Jersey publishes a gross monthly income eligibility standard set at 185% of the federal poverty level. Applications are processed by County Social Service Agencies.
program.plain_language_summary: NJ SNAP puts money on a card each month that you can use to buy groceries. Most households qualify if they earn up to 185% of the federal poverty level for their size. College students can qualify too, but they have to meet one extra rule, such as working or caring for a young child.

Are you a student, age 18 to 49 enrolled at least half-time in a college, university, community college, or business, technical, trade, or vocational school that requires a high school diploma?
If so, you may be eligible for food assistance through New Jersey’s Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP). SNAP is a federal program that can help individuals and families with low incomes buy the groceries they need to eat healthy. Eligibility depends on several factors like income, household size, resources, etc.
In addition to income eligibility factors, students also must fit at least ONE of the following requirements:
Be enrolled in an approved Career and Technical Education Program at a New Jersey community college;
Be employed at least 20 hours per week AND paid for such work;
Be participating in a federal work study program during the school year;
Be participating in an on-the-job training program;
Be responsible for the care of a member of your household who is a dependent under the age of six years-old;
Be a single parent enrolled full-time AND responsible for a dependent under the age 12 years-old;
Be unable to work due to a physical or mental disability; or
Be receiving Work First New Jersey (WFNJ) Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF) benefits (cash assistance).

Households that include a senior (aged 60 and older) or people with a disability may be eligible even if their gross income exceeds the amounts in the chart above.

program.official_name: New Jersey Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women Infants and Children (WIC)
program.description: New Jersey WIC provides supplemental foods, nutrition education and health care referrals to income eligible pregnant and postpartum women, infants and children under five years old. Applicants must live in New Jersey, provide proof of residency, meet income guidelines, and have a medical condition or limited access to nutrition that places their health at risk. Applications are made through a local WIC agency or clinic.
program.plain_language_summary: WIC gives free healthy food, nutrition advice and health referrals to pregnant people, new parents, babies and children under five. You apply through a local WIC office in New Jersey, and you will need proof of where you live and what you earn.
who_it_helps: Pregnant people
People who gave birth in the last six months
People breastfeeding a baby under a year old
Infants and children under five years old

sources.title: How to Apply for WIC
sources.excerpt:
New Jersey WIC Services are available to low and no income families as well as families experiencing unemployment, military deployment and other interim family financial hardships.
How to Apply for and Receive WIC Benefits and Services
You may apply for New Jersey WIC by contacting your local WIC agency or WIC clinic office and scheduling an appointment.
Who is Eligible to Apply for and Receive WIC Benefits?
Pregnant women
Women who have delivered a child within the last six months
Breastfeeding women who have delivered a child within the last year
Infants and children under five years old
To be eligible, people in these categories must:
Have a medical condition or limited access to nutrition that places their health at risk
Live in New Jersey and provide proof of residency
Meet income guidelines

sources.title: New Jersey WIC Services
sources.excerpt: The New Jersey Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women Infants and Children is commonly known as WIC. WIC is a successful public health nutrition program that provides wholesome food, nutrition education and community support for income eligible women who are pregnant and post-partum, infants and children up to five years old.

conditions.description: You live in New Jersey and can provide proof of residency.

program.official_name: School Nutrition Programs (National School Lunch Program and School Breakfast Program)
program.administering_org: New Jersey Department of Agriculture, Division of Food and Nutrition
program.description: The USDA school nutrition programs are administered in New Jersey by the New Jersey Department of Agriculture. Participating public schools, non-profit private schools and residential child care institutions serve nutritionally balanced low-cost or free breakfasts and lunches to children each school day. Whether an individual child pays nothing, a reduced price or the full price is determined by the school food authority, and districts with a high identified student percentage may serve all students at no cost under the Community Eligibility Provision.
program.plain_language_summary: Most New Jersey schools serve breakfast and lunch that is free or low cost. Your child's school decides who pays nothing, who pays a reduced price and who pays full price, and some schools feed every student for free. Ask the school office or the district's food service department how to apply.
who_it_helps: Families with school-age children
Children at schools that take part in the federal meal programmes

sources.title: School Nutrition Programs
sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Agriculture, Division of Food and Nutrition
sources.excerpt:
The United States Department of Agriculture’s (USDA) school nutrition programs are administered through the New Jersey Department of Agriculture (NJDA). Eligible public schools, non-profit private schools, and residential child care institutions (RCCI) enter into written agreements with NJDA to operate local programs that provide nutritionally balanced meals to children each day.
The programs available with the School Nutrition Programs include: National School Lunch Program (NSLP), School Breakfast Program (SBP), After School Snack Program (ASSP), Fresh Fruit and Vegetable Program (FFVP), Special Milk Program (SMP), and Seamless Summer Option (SSO).

program.description: The Summer Food Service Program provides free nutritious meals and snacks to children during the summer months when school is out. Approved sponsors - school districts, local government agencies, camps and private nonprofit organisations - serve the meals at central sites such as schools and community centres. At an open site, which operates where at least half of the children come from families with incomes at or below 185 percent of the federal poverty level, meals are served free to any child.
program.plain_language_summary: In the summer, kids 18 and under can get free meals and snacks at schools, community centres and other sites around New Jersey. At most sites there is no application and no income check - any child can eat.
who_it_helps: Children 18 and younger
Families with children during school breaks
People over 18 with disabilities who are in school programmes

sources.title: Summer Food Service Program
sources.publisher: New Jersey Department of Agriculture, Division of Food and Nutrition
sources.excerpt:
Children 18 and younger may receive free meals and snacks through SFSP. Meals and snacks are also available to persons with disabilities, over age 18, who participate in school programs for people who are mentally or physically disabled.

Open sites operate in low-income areas where at least half of the children come from families with incomes at or below 185 percent of the Federal poverty level, making them eligible for free and reduced price school meals. Meals are served free to any child at the open site.

conditions.description: You are in New Jersey, where the summer meal sites operate.
You have a child aged 18 or younger.

limitations: There is no individual income test at an open site: meals are served free to any child who shows up. The 185 percent figure on the official page describes which neighbourhoods a site may operate in, not who may eat, so it is deliberately not encoded as an income rule.
The programme only runs during the summer and only where a local sponsor operates a site, so availability is seasonal and local.

program.administering_org: Rutgers University-New Brunswick, Off-Campus Living & Community Initiatives
program.description: The Rutgers Student Food Pantry provides groceries, personal care items and household supplies to Rutgers-New Brunswick students at the College Avenue Student Center, through the Knight's Pantry Basic Needs Box lockers at four student centres, and through a mobile pantry that visits the Douglass, Busch and Livingston campuses. Students register in PantrySoft and may use one pantry method once per week.

ATTENTION!!! - Create an account on PantrySoft prior to stopping by the food pantry. If you need assistance, we also have tablets available to register on in the pantry. Students are able to use only one of the following food pantry methods once per week.
Rutgers Student Food Pantry
College Avenue Student Center, 126 College Ave, New Brunswick, NJ 08901 Room 112
All students must make an appointment in the PantrySoft system ahead of time if they wish to visit between the hours of 12pm-4pm (M-F), unless they are a first-time visitor. Appointments can be made for the current week starting on Sundays at noon. From 4pm-5 or 4pm-7pm we will have open walk-in hours available. Students may visit the pantry, lockers, or the mobile pantry once per week. Access to the Knights Pantry is contingent on the building hours of the student center.

program.description: The Community FoodBank of New Jersey supplies and coordinates a network of more than 800 partner agencies across eleven New Jersey counties, including food pantries, soup kitchens and shelters. Its Find Food tool maps nearby partner locations, and its staff also help residents apply for or recertify SNAP benefits. Residents of other counties are served by neighbouring food banks.
